title: unify-terraform-private-state-layout-gpu-iam-networking-migration
author: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: our Private Terraform state layout for GPU node pools, IAM roles, and VPC networking has diverged across environments causing brittle upgrades and manual state moves. This PR unifies the state layout and Terraform module interfaces so tooling and the private-installer can perform deterministic upgrades. Changes: 1) Introduce a single state layout module (modules/private-state-layout) that consolidates role, network, and node pool state scoping; 2) Refactor gpu-node-pool module to be composable with new state layout (preserve backwards-compatible inputs where possible); 3) Add explicit IAM role module changes to support per-tenant role scoping and predictable resource addresses; 4) Add migration utilities (scripts/terraform/migrate_state.sh and a TF plan parser) used by the operator to apply state moves with a dry-run mode; 5) Update examples and README with step-by-step migration instructions and rollback plan; 6) Add acceptance tests that run a dry-run state move in CI. Migration strategy: the PR includes a deterministic state mapping table and an idempotent migration script that uses terraform state mv under a lock, plus a verification plan that compares before/after resource counts and outputs. We test the migration end-to-end in the staging account using a two-step process: freeze writes to the target workspace, run script with --dry-run, and finally apply with last-resort manual approval. Rollback and safety: all migration actions are reversible because the mapping is symmetric and the script supports "undo" which moves resources back to original addresses and re-applies the previous workspace state from a snapshot. Backwards-compatibility: modules accept legacy input names via deprecated variables with warnings to make rollout non-disruptive. Impact: this reduces manual intervention during Private upgrades and enables future automation (installer upgrades and Helm charts) to rely on a stable state layout. Related: ENG-1724, INF-598. Risk: state migrations are high-impact; this PR includes a staged rollout doc and a canary path that migrates a single tenant first. Testing notes: unit tests for modules, integration tests in staging account, and manual verification logs attached.
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) add modules/private-state-layout plus docs and tests; 2) refactor modules/gpu-node-pool to new state layout and add compatibility shims; 3) add scripts/terraform/migrate_state.sh and CI dry-run pipeline
review_comments: Aisha: Please add a safety check that prevents running the final apply against production without an explicit flag. Author: added --force-production flag and updated docs.
Daniel: The terraform provider lockfile changed, CI failed on initial run. Author: bumped provider lockfile and pinned provider versions in modules, re-ran CI.

Martin: Can we avoid changing resource addresses for existing iam roles to preserve external references? Author: added alias variables and preserved resource addresses via lifecycle and mapping so external references stay valid.
release_notes: Private Terraform: unify state layout for GPU node pools, IAM, and networking to enable deterministic migrations; add migration script and staging dry-run CI; compatibility shims included to avoid breaking existing deployments.
notes_for_ops: Run scripts/terraform/migrate_state.sh --dry-run against staging workspace, verify outputs, then run with --execute and --force-production only with two approvals. Snapshot workspace state before final apply.
security_implications: No secrets changed. IAM role scoping tightened; reviewers verified policies to avoid privilege expansion.
observability_changes: Adds migration metrics (migration.duration, migration.status) emitted to ops pipeline during migration runs.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for modules, integration dry-run ran in CI against a mocked state, staging run verified resource counts matched expected mapping.
